P1.finding: M1301.execute_once verifies the M1301-pinned M1297 triplet and M1298 seals, validates the repaired claims, then calls M1297.execute_once directly. Frozen M1297.main, however, first calls M1297.M.verify_frozen_authorities(), which pins the M1257 source/test/contract triplet. M1297.execute_once does not call that inherited preflight, so the additive wrapper silently removes it.
P1.impact: The executable M1257 source remains transitively SHA-pinned at import, so this is not an arbitrary-code P0. It is nevertheless a production authority-chain regression: M1257 test/contract identity drift is no longer rejected at the same gate as frozen M1297 production.
P1.reproduction: The independent test injects an inherited-preflight failure and observes M1301 delegation return normally with zero calls to M1297.M.verify_frozen_authorities().
P1.required_fix: Create an additive successor that pins M1301 and calls frozen M1297.M.verify_frozen_authorities() after its own M1301 authority and exact-claim checks and before M1297.execute_once. Preserve all current entity/FD/snapshot/attempt behavior, then obtain a fresh different-author hammer.
